$comment: DDL adapter for Claude Code (protocol §2.5). The rule against mutation without approval always applies. After detecting a +++DDL_REPORT and until submitted human input, the gate guards only tool calls covered by PreToolUse. Its catch-all matcher permits known safe reads, human questions, and bounded literal shell reads; mutating calls, unknown tools, and worker follow-ups are denied on those paths. The processor decides whether an actual submitted answer approves the current report and scope. Turn termination remains an instruction; running processes and hook-bypassing transports are outside this guard. Protocol §2.5 records the asynchronous transcript and fail-open limits. The spawn depth of 1 keeps worker starts with the lead. Native push confirmation depends on the active permission policy and is additional to approval in the /commit report. Commits carry no AI attribution. The rules live in the commands and protocol and remain instructions where the adapter is absent or cannot enforce them. Ordinary Git commit/push calls additionally require the prepared content review matched to the actual native submission and Git snapshot, even while STOP is open or native permission prompts are suppressed. An unreadable or mismatched Git review denies recognized calls. Runtime-level hook failures and timeouts remain outside that guarantee.
